chunks: And regarding the hip: if it breaks and is set without a defect or flaw, its compensation is one-fifth of the wergild of the leg, which is one hundred dinars. And if the hip is fractured, its compensation is one hundred and sixty dinars, which is four-fifths of the wergild of its breaking. If it is exposed, its compensation is one-quarter of the wergild of its breaking, which is fifty dinars. And the compensation for the displacement of its bones is one hundred and seventy-five dinars: from this, one hundred dinars is for its break, fifty dinars for the displacement of its bones, and twenty-five dinars for its exposure. And the compensation for its disjointing is thirty dinars. So if it is bruised and becomes defective, its compensation is three hundred and thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar.

key_terms.عَثْمٌ: A specific type of bone fracture or defect

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah (blood money) for a broken or injured hip bone according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage from al-Kafi outlines the precise monetary compensation (diyah) for various degrees of hip bone injury, reflecting the systematic approach of Shia jurisprudence to bodily damages. It distinguishes between simple fractures, displacement, and exposure, assigning specific dinar amounts that often correspond to fractional shares of the total leg wergild, thereby ensuring equitable restitution based on the extent of the harm.
